content:
Soojin Lee: putting final touches on the demo deck v1 today. can we get ONE set of benchmark numbers we can use consistently across slides? (latency + cost + throughput) 

Soojin Lee: specifically for the “production economics” section we currently have 3 different numbers floating around in drafts and it’s getting messy. need approved figures + caveats (what hardware/model/seq length/etc). 

Camila Reyes: +1. also need to know what we can say out loud vs what has to be “internal only”. slide needs something like “up to X tok/s” and “$Y per 1M tokens” but with safe footnotes.

Dylan Brooks: jumping in — for the live demo we should anchor on numbers that reflect what the demo tenant actually shows in Console (token-level breakdown + p50/p95). if we pick something too aggressive and the dashboard shows different, it’ll look bad.

Logan Wright: fwiw a lot of drift is from people mixing (a) single-request latency vs (b) throughput under batching vs (c) e2e including network. we should define: client→server→client, region=us-west-2, streaming on, and a fixed prompt/response shape.

Sean Gallagher: + caveat that these are “illustrative” and workload dependent. pls don’t put anything that reads like an SLA. for demo deck we can use “typical” ranges and “as measured in Redwood demo env” language.

Markus Klein: what’s the decision: do we want numbers for (1) Hosted API baseline and (2) Optimized (batching + cache + quant) so we can show the delta? that seems consistent with the story.

Soojin Lee: yes exactly. baseline vs optimized, and the story is “same quality target, lower unit cost + predictable latency.”

Alex Martinez: for dev-facing credibility, can we tie it to an example workload? e.g., “customer support chat: prompt ~1k tokens, output ~250 tokens” (or whatever is our demo script). then the numbers aren’t random.

Ethan Park: I can share what we’ve been using in internal perf notes, but we need to be careful about model version pin + hardware. 

Ethan Park: suggestion: pick one Redwood-verified model in the deck (the same one we pin for demo routes). then specify: “Pinned to model X @ version Y in demo tenant. Hardware: H100 80GB. Region: us-west. Measurements include queueing + generation, exclude client-side rendering.”

Camila Reyes: can someone give the actual numbers though :)

Logan Wright: ok here’s a proposal for deck-safe figures (NOT a guarantee):
- Workload: 1,024 input tokens, 256 output tokens, temperature 0.2, streaming on
- Region: us-west
- Model: Redwood-verified “RWI-Large-Instruct” (pinned)
Baseline (no caching, conservative batching):
- p50 time-to-first-token (TTFT): ~250–350ms
- p50 end-to-end completion latency: ~2.0–2.6s
- p95 end-to-end completion latency: ~3.8–5.0s
- Throughput: ~70–110 tok/s per GPU equivalent (varies with concurrency)
Optimized (prefix/KV cache on + continuous batching tuned):
- p50 TTFT: ~180–260ms
- p50 end-to-end completion latency: ~1.4–2.0s
- p95 end-to-end completion latency: ~2.8–3.9s
- Throughput: ~110–170 tok/s per GPU equivalent

Logan Wright: cost: we should be careful because pricing varies by SKU and customer commit. but we can state a unit economics example as “relative improvement” (e.g., “20–35% lower cost per generated token with caching/batching on typical chat workloads”).

Soojin Lee: these ranges are helpful. can we give one number for the slide headline? ranges in speaker notes.

Sean Gallagher: +1 on ranges in notes. for headline, pick something conservative and call it “typical p50”.

Mina Haddad: also please avoid mixing in fallback routing metrics. the reliability story has different numbers (failover adds latency). keep perf story clean.

Dylan Brooks: for Console alignment: I’d rather we use “p50 completion latency ~2.3s baseline / ~1.7s optimized” (same workload) because that’s close to what the seeded synthetic traffic shows today.

Camila Reyes: can we also include a “cost per 1M tokens” illustrative number? customers ask for it immediately.

Ethan Park: if we put $/1M tokens in the deck, it will be screenshot and forwarded around. we should avoid hard dollar figures unless we’re ok with it being used out of context.

Soojin Lee: ok, so maybe keep $ out of slides and say “token-level cost breakdown in Console + levers to reduce cost” with a % improvement callout.

Camila Reyes: I’m ok with that. we can keep a “pricing guidance” appendix for reps.

Logan Wright: recommendation for slide copy (approved-ish wording):
Headline:
- “Typical p50 completion latency: ~2.3s → ~1.7s (with caching + tuned batching)”
Sub-bullets:
- “Token-level cost visibility + levers to reduce unit cost (often 20–35% on repeat/prefix-heavy workloads)”
Footnote:
- “Illustrative benchmark. Workload: 1,024 in / 256 out tokens, streaming on, us-west. Demo tenant pinned model + version. Results vary by model, context length, and concurrency.”

Sean Gallagher: + add “as of <month/year>” so it doesn’t get treated as evergreen.

Markus Klein: I’ll sync with the demo tenant seed data so the dashboards show these numbers (or within band). would rather we adjust the synthetic load than have a mismatch.

Alex Martinez: can we add a short line in speaker notes: “ask prospect what their typical prompt/response sizes are” so we can contextualize why theirs will differ.

Soojin Lee: perfect. action items:
- Logan: send final “deck-safe” numbers + footnote text in a single blurb I can paste
- Markus: confirm demo tenant dashboard baselines align
- Camila: remove $ figures from slides, keep % improvement + point to pricing appendix

Logan Wright: will DM a paste-ready blurb in ~15 mins.

Camila Reyes: thank you. will update the deck doc once we have the exact wording.

Sean Gallagher: pls also include “not an SLA” language in internal notes for reps. (doesn’t need to be on the slide, but in the talk track doc).

Soojin Lee: noted. adding to talk track.
